chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Sa'id, from a man who asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):
Regarding a man who bequeathed twenty dirhams for Hajj, he said: 'A man should perform Hajj on his behalf using that money, from wherever he can find him.'

key_terms.مِنْ حَيْثُ يَبْلُغُهُ: from wherever he can be found/reached

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone bequeaths money specifically for Hajj after their death?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *Hajj al-Tamattu'* or *Hajj al-Badal* (substitute pilgrimage) funded by the deceased's estate, emphasizing the practical execution of the bequest. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the specific intent of the testator is honored by appointing a capable representative to perform the ritual, ensuring the spiritual debt is discharged. This ruling underscores the importance of fulfilling religious obligations even after death, a key concept in Shia inheritance and worship jurisprudence.
